$comment: Per-entrypoint bundle-size budgets for @honua/sdk-js (issue #350).
Each budget is a hard byte ceiling for a single public entrypoint bundled the
way a real consumer would build it: esbuild --bundle --minify, target es2020,
runtime peers (maplibre-gl, cesium, @bufbuild/*, @connectrpc/*) kept external.
'min' is the minified byte size; 'gzip' is the gzip-compressed byte size.
HEADROOM POLICY: budgets are set to the measured current size + ~10% headroom
(ceil(actual * 1.1)). The 10% absorbs normal churn without hiding real bloat.
When a legitimate change pushes an entry over budget, re-run
'npm run report:bundle-sizes' to refresh docs/bundle-sizes.md, then RESET that
entry's budget to the new actual + ~10% in the SAME PR (never widen silently).
'npm run verify:bundle-budgets' is the CI gate; it fails on any exceedance with
a per-entry delta table.
'tree-shake:HonuaClient' is a deep-import-hygiene guard: a fixture importing ONLY
{ HonuaClient } from the root entry must stay under its ceiling, proving a single
symbol does not drag the whole SDK into a consumer bundle.

/source-schema is the focused experimental SourceSchemaV2 runtime, including the pinned PROJJSON validator. 'tree-shake:root-connect' proves default root discovery does not retain that validation stack. Both ceilings are measured actual plus ~10% headroom.

/geoparquet was reset for bounded GeoParquet 1.0/1.1 projection validation (exact versions, geometry types, bbox, epoch, and covering checks): 22,092 minified / 7,889 gzip bytes. /map's gzip ceiling was reset after the lightweight structural SourceSchemaV2 envelope check reached its shared discovery path: 42,656 gzip bytes. Ceilings are measured actual plus ~10% headroom; root, /honua, browser, /contract, and /query-planner ceilings remain unchanged.

/react and /geometry landed with the adoption-wave-1 bundle (issues #349/#351). /esri-compat's budget was reset for the geometryEngine shim's turf/proj4 backing; 'tree-shake:esri-compat-FeatureLayerCompat' guards that compat consumers who never touch geometryEngine keep paying only the pre-shim cost. 'tree-shake:geometry-buffer' is intentionally large: @turf/buffer carries a JSTS port (~66 KiB gzip); light ops like area() shake down to ~1 KiB.

/map was reset for the accepted-plan source workflow (#390): 62.6 to 79.5 KiB min and 16.2 to 21.8 KiB gzip after removing the generic aggregate executor. Keeping the adapter on /map preserves the canonical endpoint-to-map import; 'tree-shake:map-source-workflow' isolates its 17.1 KiB min / 6.4 KiB gzip consumer cost.

/contract gzip was reset for credential-safe discovery (#391): provider-aware Azure SAS, CloudFront, AWS, and GCS signed-URL normalization plus runtime evidence-kind validation. The measured 61,493 bytes gzip is budgeted at 67,643 bytes per the 10% headroom policy.

/realtime gained its first dedicated guard with the resumable checkpoint kernel (#393); its trust-boundary hardening adds runtime event validation and credential-free envelope projection. The ceiling is the measured subpath bundle plus 10% headroom.

/offline is a subpath-only experimental contract (#396), keeping the root/browser bundle unchanged while its dedicated budget guards deterministic region and edit-replay growth. The budget was reset for acknowledged one-pass replay (#914): strict edit/request/idempotency binding, bounded transport invocation, cancellation, credential-free receipts, and all queue primitives measure 85,533 minified / 23,740 gzip bytes. Both ceilings are measured actual plus 10% headroom, and root/browser barrels remain unchanged.

/query-planner gained its first dedicated guard with the bounded columnar worker session (#453); browser/Node worker implementations and heavy analytics peers remain injected, while the full planner plus worker protocol is measured with 10% headroom.

/query-planner was reset for the DuckDB SQL and gRPC query compilers plus spatial-aggregation pushdown (#389): the DuckDB compiler reuses the dependency-free geoparquet-sql builder so planner and adapter emit identical SQL. Measured 75,024 minified / 22,254 gzip; the ceiling is actual plus ~10% headroom.

/query-planner gzip was reset for deterministic columnar worker aggregation (#939): the first reducing columnar operation adds dictionary/temporal/spatial-grid grouping, count/sum/min/max/mean accumulation over packed buffers, compensated summation, and the honua.aggregate result layout and reader. Measured 151,363 gzip bytes; the ceiling is actual plus ~10% headroom. No new dependency enters the entrypoint's static graph — #939 NFR-004 keeps Arrow, DuckDB, and projection peers out — and the minified ceiling stayed below its existing value, so only the exceeded gzip ceiling was reset.

/query-planner's gzip ceiling was reset for realtime columnar patch semantics (#941): applyColumnarPatch adds the versioned append/update/delete patch contract, feature-id identity resolution, reserved-capacity in-place writes, the bounded tombstone overlay, the four declared rebuild thresholds, and the compacting buffer-level rebuild. Measured on the tree merged with #1023's persistent batch cache and #1029's batch-to-Result conversion: 170,267 gzip bytes with the module's two export blocks wired in and 157.3 KiB without them, so the module itself costs about 9.0 KiB gzip. Only the exceeded gzip ceiling is reset, to measured actual plus ~10% headroom. The minified ceiling this branch carried before the merge (798,849) was dropped as redundant: the merged entrypoint measures 740.5 KiB minified against 707.7 KiB without the module, and that sits inside the 797,370 ceiling #940 established, so trunk's value stands. No new dependency enters the entrypoint's static graph — the patch path reuses the same dependency-free GeoArrow encode/inspect primitives — and root, /honua, and browser barrels are unchanged because the columnar surface remains subpath-only.

/agent-safety was reset again for binding safety authorization to accepted-plan and discovery evidence (#468): derived accepted-evidence gating over the approved execution/audit boundary (#456) measures 51,401 minified / 14,693 gzip bytes; each ceiling is actual plus 10% headroom and the code remains out of root barrels.

Gzip remained below its existing ceiling; only the exceeded minified ceilings were reset to measured actual plus 10% headroom.

The optional scene entrypoint ceiling is measured actual plus 10% headroom; Cesium remains external and dynamically imported, while root and browser entrypoints stay within their existing ceilings.

The subpath is experimental and subpath-only — root and browser barrels are unchanged.

/controls and /web-components gained their first dedicated guards with the app-platform component-kit qualification matrix (#683, NFR-001). Both are budgeted at measured actual plus ~10% headroom, measured after the production-tier feature editor (#680) merged into the kit: /controls at 856,712 minified / 232,443 gzip and /web-components at 906,215 / 246,711. The feature editor is the difference between these numbers and the pre-merge measurement (834,812 / 225,597 and 838,769 / 227,166); the ceilings were reset in the merge rather than left at their original values, so the entries keep the full 10% headroom the policy intends instead of starting life ~1% under. Both entries additionally forbid a renderer, PDF writer, image encoder, localization framework, or test-only peer as a static input, which is the packaging half of NFR-001 -- secure export reaches all of those through the application-supplied adapter seam. /controls is measured pessimistically on purpose: src/controls/registry.ts reaches the web-components kit through a dynamic import() so a controls-only consumer never pays for it (a real Rollup/Vite build emits a separate lazy chunk), but this measurement folds dynamic imports into one graph, so the ceiling covers the worst case in which a consumer registers a web-components-sourced tag. Reducing that ceiling is tracked with the rest of epic #678's bundle work, not silently widened here.

Application Experience GA (#1294) adds the shared application context, bounded feature inspection, mutation receipts/offline editing integration, table aggregation and secure export, and executable qualification metadata. Measured /controls at 1,078,673 minified / 291,096 gzip bytes and /web-components at 1,180,514 minified / approximately 314.1 KiB gzip. Only the exceeded /controls min+gzip and /web-components min ceilings are reset to measured actual plus 10% headroom; /web-components gzip remains under its existing ceiling, and renderer/localization/test peers remain forbidden static inputs.

Each ceiling is measured actual plus ~10% headroom.

The subpath remains experimental and subpath-only — root and browser barrels are unchanged.

Measured 31,977 minified / 10,209 gzip; both ceilings are measured actual plus ~10% headroom. The subpath remains experimental and subpath-only — root and browser barrels are unchanged.

The shared profile registration/schema-binding guard measures 49,916 minified / 15,612 gzip bytes; ceilings are measured actual plus 10% headroom.
